Table 1. Weight misspecification (non-null GWAS)

Per-replicate percentage change in r2 with the true genetic value when PRS-MIX uses a weight off from w0 by the column offset, relative to PRS-MIX at w0; negative values mean lower accuracy. The change is relative, r2(w)/r2(w0) − 1 per replicate, so the threshold is a fraction of the generating-weight r2, not an absolute difference. Bold: the lower 95% bound falls below −2%, the acceptable relative loss fixed before the curves were examined; unbolded cells are within it. –: the weight is outside [0, 1]. Exploratory analysis, not curated paper evidence. Chromosome 22, fixed 250 kb LD blocks, PRS-CS with automatic φ and default sampler settings; replicates 1–20 per setting. w0 is the generating weight on the first-listed ancestry; PRS-MIX at w = 1 and 0 is first- and second-ancestry PRS-CS. Square brackets are pointwise 95% t intervals over replicates, paired within replicate; they are exploratory and not adjusted for the number of settings and weights.

Table 3. Recovery of the composition by null LD fit

Per replicate, the weight in 0, 0.1, …, 1 that minimises the Gaussian LD-fit loss (ridge 0.001) of the mixed panel against the null GWAS z-scores; mean (Monte Carlo SE) over replicates. The null GWAS is simulated separately from the non-null GWAS in Tables 1, 2 and 4, so this asks only whether LD fit recovers the composition; it does not validate LD fit as a way to choose the weight for prediction. Exploratory analysis, not curated paper evidence. Chromosome 22, fixed 250 kb LD blocks, PRS-CS with automatic φ and default sampler settings; replicates 1–20 per setting. w0 is the generating weight on the first-listed ancestry; PRS-MIX at w = 1 and 0 is first- and second-ancestry PRS-CS. Square brackets are pointwise 95% t intervals over replicates, paired within replicate; they are exploratory and not adjusted for the number of settings and weights.

Table 4. Oracle benchmarks (retrospective)

The weight with the highest mean r2, and the better of the two single panels, both chosen with the true genetic values of the same target individuals; mean (Monte Carlo SE). These choices are not available to a user and are optimistic by construction; they show how much a perfectly informed choice could gain over the generating weight.
